sentence_stem: If I had studied harder last year,
correct_completion: I would have a better job now.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder last year, I would have a better job now.
acceptable_variants: I would be earning more money now.
I would be in a better position today.

options.text: I will study harder next year.
options.why_wrong: This is a plan for the future. It does not describe the imagined past condition and its present result.

options.text: I would have a better job now.

options.why_wrong: The present simple describes a habit and does not connect to the imagined past condition.

options.text: I had a better job last year.
options.why_wrong: This is a past simple statement about a real past event, not an imagined present result.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals: past perfect in the if-clause and 'would' for a present result
explanation: This is a mixed conditional. The if-clause describes a past situation with the past perfect 'had studied', while the main clause describes a present result with 'would have ... now'. Portuguese speakers often copy the same tense into both clauses, but English keeps the past perfect in the if-clause and uses 'would' for the present result.
translation: Se eu tivesse estudado mais no ano passado, eu teria um emprego melhor agora.
